originalTitle: Oil prices fall after U.S. says crude exports through Strait of Hormuz near 9 million barrels per day
summary: Oil futures retreated early Wednesday morning after prices rose overnight.
content:
Oil prices fell Thursday after Energy Secretary Chris Wright claimed that exports through the Strait of Hormuz are higher than many independent estimates.

U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures fell 2.4% to close at $81.25 per barrel. Brent crude, the international benchmark, lost about 2% to settle at $87.07. Prices are up about 4% this week as a deal between Washington and Tehran to increase ship traffic through Hormuz still has not materialized.

Oil exports through Hormuz have neared a seven-day average of 9 million barrels per day, Wright said Wednesday. Exports from the Gulf rise to around 15 million bpd when pipeline flows are included, he said. About 20 million bpd of oil and products moved through Hormuz before the war.

The export data provided by the energy secretary is much higher than the estimates of many independent firms. TD Securities, for example, has put Hormuz exports at around 5 million bpd. This is "nowhere near enough for the market," said Ryan McKay, director of commodity strategy at the firm, in a Wednesday note.

Wright said in a social media post Wednesday that the U.S. military and Department of Energy maintain "the best available data related to oil and oil products leaving the Arabian gulf."

"Many private businesses undercount the number of ships leaving the Strait of Hormuz due to ships moving covertly through the waterway," he said.

Oil demand is expected to fall by 1.6 million barrels per day this year, about 510,000 bpd more than previously anticipated , according to the International Energy Agency . Renewed hostilities in the Gulf have undermined efforts to boost global oil supplies, the IEA said. Supply was 6.3 million bpd lower year-on-year in July with 8.3 million bpd of Gulf production shut in, it said.

The security situation in the Middle East remains precarious for shippers, with attacks on vessels in the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea this week. Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen, meanwhile, claimed Thursday that they targeted a refinery in Saudi Arabia's Jizan region with drones.

The U.S. and Iran disputed who controls Hormuz this week. Tehran claims that it has closed the strait and it will only reopen the waterway after Washington meets its demands. President Donald Trump, meanwhile, claimed the U.S. has total control over Hormuz.

The Trump administration last week teased a potential deal with Iran to boost traffic through the strait, but an agreement still has not materialized.

"The one thing we know is we have to discount political statements. They're completely irrelevant to what's happening," Amos Hochstein, a former energy advisory to President Joe Biden, told CNBC Thursday. "It's all nonsense. It's just market management."
chineseTitle: 美国表示通过霍尔木兹海峡的原油出口量接近每天 900 万桶，导致油价下跌
chineseSummary: 隔夜价格上涨后，石油期货周三早间回落。
chineseContent:
能源部长克里斯赖特声称通过霍尔木兹海峡的出口高于许多独立估计后，周四油价下跌。

美国西德克萨斯中质原油期货下跌 2.4%，收于每桶 81.25 美元。国际基准布伦特原油下跌约 2%，收于 87.07 美元。由于华盛顿和德黑兰之间关于增加霍尔木兹海峡船舶流量的协议尚未落实，本周价格上涨了约 4%。

赖特周三表示，通过霍尔木兹的石油出口已接近 7 天平均每天 900 万桶。他表示，如果算上管道流量，海湾地区的出口量将增至每天 1500 万桶左右。战前，每天约有 2000 万桶石油和产品通过霍尔木兹运输。

能源部长提供的出口数据远高于许多独立公司的估计。例如，道明证券预计霍尔木兹油田的出口量约为每日 500 万桶。该公司大宗商品策略总监瑞安·麦凯(Ryan McKay)在周三的一份报告中表示，这“对市场来说还远远不够”。

赖特周三在社交媒体帖子中表示，美国军方和能源部保留“与离开阿拉伯湾的石油和石油产品有关的最佳可用数据”。

他说：“由于船只秘密通过该水道，许多私营企业低估了离开霍尔木兹海峡的船只数量。”

据国际能源署称，今年石油需求预计将减少 160 万桶/日，比此前预期多约 51 万桶/日。国际能源署表示，海湾地区重新爆发的敌对行动削弱了增加全球石油供应的努力。 7月份供应量同比减少630万桶/日，海湾地区产量关闭830万桶/日。

中东的安全局势对托运人来说仍然不稳定，本周阿曼湾和红海的船只遭到袭击。与此同时，伊朗在也门的胡塞盟友周四声称，他们用无人机瞄准了沙特阿拉伯吉赞地区的一家炼油厂。

美国和伊朗本周就谁控制霍尔木兹海峡产生争议。德黑兰声称已关闭该海峡，只有在华盛顿满足其要求后才会重新开放该水道。与此同时，唐纳德·特朗普总统声称美国完全控制霍尔木兹海峡。

特朗普政府上周暗示可能与伊朗达成协议，以增加海峡交通，但协议尚未落实。

“我们知道的一件事是，我们必须忽视政治声明。它们与正在发生的事情完全无关，”乔·拜登总统的前能源顾问阿莫斯·霍赫斯坦周四告诉 CNBC。 “这都是无稽之谈。这只是市场管理。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
